text:
Sam: Heads-up — Vendor 'NordicCloud AS' sent an invoice for consulting (NO). They haven't charged VAT but are now asking us to gross-up the payment to cover a Norwegian withholding tax they say applies. Any guidance before I reply? :thinking:

Claire: Do we have their VAT/ORG number on file? AP, did you classify them as Norway vendor?

Sam: Invoice snippet: ```
Invoice: 2026-03-12
From: NordicCloud AS
Org number: 921 234 567
Amount: EUR 8,500
Line: Professional services - remote infra support
Note from vendor: "We expect a 15% withholding; please gross up so we receive net amount after Norwegian WHT."
```

Claire: We only have a bare onboarding record, no VAT ID captured in Coupa. I flagged for AP review. Please don't pay until we confirm. :eyes:

Ivan: A few quick points — Norway isn't in the EU but is in EEA; VAT and withholding are separate regimes. For B2B cross-border services the buyer is often liable for VAT via reverse charge, but that depends on which Redwood legal entity is being invoiced and the service type. Withholding (WHT) in Norway can apply to certain payments to non-residents, but it's unusual for standard consulting/SaaS unless it's treated as royalties or specific taxable services.

Ivan: Also — W-8/W-9 are US forms and not applicable here. If the vendor wants us to gross-up, that is a commercial request. Our standard policy: we do not gross-up vendor invoices unless there's an explicit contract clause or a local tax ruling. We need: vendor's Norwegian tax cert or written tax assessment showing WHT applies, and confirmation which Redwood entity is the payer. We should also ask vendor to reissue invoice indicating VAT treatment (0% reverse charge) if appropriate.

Anna: Confirming — who is the invoiced entity on the PDF? That determines reverse charge vs. import VAT. Sam?

Sam: It says "Redwood Ltd" with a UK billing address. So vendor is invoicing Redwood UK Ltd.

Ivan: If it's Redwood UK Ltd being invoiced by a Norway supplier, the UK import VAT rules and reverse charge for services apply. Vendor shouldn't be withholding UK tax. Norway withholding on services to the UK is possible in rare cases but vendor needs to show legal basis. Bottom line: don't gross-up. Request documentation. If vendor insists we can escalate to Legal to see contract basis.

Claire: Action for AP: hold payment, request from vendor: (1) copy of Norway tax registration / confirmation of WHT claim; (2) legal basis and amount calculation if they insist on WHT; (3) reissued invoice showing VAT/VAT-exemption or reverse-charge wording. I'll create the ticket and email vendor this afternoon.

Sam: I'll copy Legal and Tax on my reply. Sample reply I'll send: "Thanks — we cannot gross-up. Please provide tax/legal documentation that demonstrates Norwegian WHT applies to this payment and reissue invoice with clear VAT treatment. If there's a contract clause, attach it. Payment will be held until we receive these."

Anna: Sounds good. Tag me when they respond so Legal can check contract language.

invoice-bot: Payment status updated: HOLD set for invoice 2026-03-12 (NordicCloud AS) by Claire — reason: tax documentation requested.

Sam: Thanks everyone — I'll send the vendor note now and paste their reply here.
